Question B-005-010-005.

Why the correct answer is right: In an AC circuit, impedance is the ratio of AC voltage to AC current. It includes resistance and any reactance in the circuit.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Resistance": Resistance is only the non-reactive part and does not cover capacitive or inductive effects.
- sourceIndex 2: "Reactance": Reactance is frequency-dependent opposition alone; impedance is the combined voltage-current ratio.
- sourceIndex 3: "Conductance": Conductance describes ease of current flow, so it is the inverse idea rather than the voltage-to-current opposition.
